raw_response:
*speaking as the farmer, in my own voice*

Aiya, this year again stevia. Thirty years I've been on this land, the last seven or eight I've been doing stevia because the contractor from the company comes and buys it up, and for one mu and a bit you can't make anything worth the trouble on wheat-maize. With only 1.1 mu, if I did wheat-maize like my neighbors, after all the costs I'd barely have enough to eat, let alone put something aside. My two sons work outside — one in Handan, one further south — so they send money home, but this little piece of land is still mine to manage, and stevia brings in more cash per mu than grain, as long as the leaves come out clean and green.

The company gives us the seedlings on credit — they take it back out when they weigh the dry leaves at the end. I think last year it was about 350 yuan of seedlings for my mu-plus, something like that. I don't need to buy seed myself, which is good because I don't have much cash sitting around in spring.

Planting I'll do end of April, maybe first few days of May, depending on when the ground warms up and when the seedlings arrive. My wife and I can set them out ourselves in two days, maybe three — my daughter-in-law helps if she's around. The rows I do like everybody in our village, about a chi and a half apart, seedling every half chi or so.

Fertilizer — I put down compound fertilizer before planting, maybe two bags (that's about 40 kg) on the whole 1.1 mu, the 15-15-15 kind. Then after the first cut in July I sprinkle some urea, maybe half a bag, to push the second growth. Last year I tried a little more urea and the leaves got too soft, the company docked my price, so this year I go back to what I used to do. My neighbor old Wang does similar, he's been at stevia longer than me.

Water — I have the tube well share with three other households. Stevia doesn't like to dry out, the leaves get bitter. I irrigate before planting to soften the ground, then maybe three more times during summer if it doesn't rain enough. Pumping costs add up, the electricity and the share of the well fee, so I don't water more than I have to. If it rains good in July and August I might only pump twice.

Pests — some caterpillars eat the leaves sometimes, and there's a leaf spot disease that showed up two years ago. I spray once or twice if I see problems, nothing if the crop looks clean. I don't want chemical on the leaves close to harvest, the company tests for it.

Tillage is simple — I hire the small tractor fellow to turn over my little plot, costs me maybe 50 yuan. One pass is enough, then I rake by hand.

Harvest is the hard part. Two cuts, sometimes three if the weather stays warm into September. First cut around end of June or early July, second cut in August, third cut September if it's still growing. I cut with a sickle, spread leaves on the yard at home to dry, turn them every day. Three or four dry days and they're ready. My wife and I do all of it ourselves — this is only 1.1 mu, no need to hire anyone. If I had ten mu of this I'd be in trouble.

Yield — last year I got about 180 kg of dry leaves off my 1.1 mu, so maybe 160 kg per mu. Year before was better, closer to 200 per mu, but the August was dry. This year I'm hoping for 170 or so per mu, can't count on more than that at my age with just the two of us working.
